concept: Input is a window recessed into the appliance's body that takes text: a well the full width of its column, the light falling into it from the top left, with its name printed above on the inset line like the printing on a case.

default_to_avoid.pattern: Material outlined text field: a bordered 8px-radius input rectangle with a floating label
default_to_avoid.why_not: A floating label shrinks into the border and doubles as a placeholder, while P5 prints every label flat on the inset line above its part.

default_to_avoid.pattern: input whose placeholder is the only label
default_to_avoid.why_not: The placeholder disappears the moment someone types, so the field loses its name exactly when it is being filled in.

references.source: Braun ET 66 calculator (Dietrich Lubs, 1987): the entry window is a recess in the body, its figures read inside the frame
Braun T 1000 world receiver (Dieter Rams, 1963): band names printed above each window and scale on the case
system/FORM.md input class: recessed well, full width of its column, label printed above on the inset line

derivation.consequence: the window is recessed into the body (inverse light)
derivation.form: The well is surface.sunken with elevation.well, so shade sits on its top-left inner edge and the field reads as cut into the body.

derivation.consequence: the window is a rounded rectangle whose radius nests in the body
derivation.form: The well takes corner.media and stretches to the full inline size of its column, never a floating box of its own width.

derivation.consequence: labels sit on the body's inset line, never floating mid-surface
derivation.form: The label is printed above the well at its start edge, outside it, and never moves into the border or the text area.

derivation.consequence: ink on plastic at ≥4.5:1 in both themes; no tinted text
derivation.form: Typed text is text.primary on surface.sunken, the unit and hint text.secondary, all above 4.5:1 in light and dark.

derivation.consequence: links, borders, icons, selections and charts never use it
derivation.form: Focus is the shared dark ring and invalid is a red mark with a glyph and words, so the field never spends the unit's orange.

derivation.consequence: every part keeps ≥44px hit area even when it draws smaller
derivation.form: The well is at least control.md tall (44px) at md and control.lg (52px) at lg, and the line box fits stacked Thai marks.

options.name: window field, caption printed inside the well
slot field, label beside, value over a narrow groove

variants.reason: A keeps the label printed on the inset line above a full-width recess (P5 space, P2 depth); B's caption inside the well drifts toward the floating label it must avoid and needs a 60px well, and C's narrow groove reads as a fader and leaves the field short of its column.

root.why: The field stacks its label, well and message in one column so the label sits on the inset line above the well.

label.why: The printed name uses the label size in medium weight, like the printing beside every other part of the unit.

well.why: The recess takes the inverse light, shade on its top-left inner edge, so the person sees where text goes.

field.why: Typed text is primary ink on the sunken plastic at more than 4.5:1, with a line box tall enough for Thai marks.

unit.why: The printed unit sits beside the value inside the window, as the unit sits beside a reading on the display.

hint.why: The hint is secondary ink on plastic above 4.5:1, printed under the well so it never covers the value.

error.why: The error message is a red mark with a word, never the orange, which stays reserved for the unit's primary control.

glyph.why: A printed mark beside the words means invalid is never told by colour alone, for people who cannot see the red.

md.why: The default well is 44px tall, the smallest target that every part in dial keeps for a finger.

lg.why: A 52px well with larger text for the main field of a phone sheet held in one hand.

focus-within.why: The well shows the same dark ring as every part when its text area holds the keyboard focus.

data-invalid=true.why: An invalid well draws its edge in the critical red, which is never orange, and the message below names the problem.

data-disabled=true.why: A disabled field loses its recess shadow and fades to half, so it reads as not taking input right now.

@media forced-colors: active.why: In forced colours the well keeps a real border and the focus ring uses the system highlight colour.
